instruction: Place an Amazon order as per my Amazon shopping list note in SimpleNote.
notes: Flow: read passwords, log in to SimpleNote, find and read the 'Amazon shopping list' note (which lists product ids with quantities and the delivery address name), log in to Amazon, clear the cart so the order contains only the listed items, add each listed product with its quantity, look up the address id (matching the note's Home/Work name; existing addresses must not be modified) and a payment card id, place the order, then complete the task with no answer. The note's line items are runtime data: three placeholder product/quantity pairs are modelled via static (on-shopping-list ?p ?q) facts gated by the knowledge predicate (shopping-list-read); if the note has a different number of items, add/remove product, quantity objects and the matching init/goal facts. Because the number of items is variable, the per-item (in-cart ...) facts live in the goal rather than in the nullary complete-task precondition; correct ordering is still enforced structurally: add-to-cart requires (not (order-placed)), clear-cart requires (not (cart-cleared)), and complete-task requires (order-placed). The amazon.Address table must not be updated/deleted, so no address-editing actions are modelled.
